concept.concept_description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'The chromatic number of 3-stable Kneser graphs' and formalize its key results. Abstract: For an integer $s \ge 2$, a subset $S \subseteq [n]$ is {\em $s$-stable} if $\min \{j - i, n + i - j\}\ge s$ for every $i,j \in S$ with $i<j$. Denote the set of all $s$-stable subsets of size $k$ of $[n]$ by $\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}$. Schrijver proved in 1978 that whenever $n\ge 2k$, the chromatic number of the Kneser graph $\mathrm{KG}\big( \binom{[n]}{k}_{2\text{-stable}}\big)$ is $n - 2k +2$. Generalizing this result, Meunier conjectured in 2011 that $χ\left( \mathrm{KG}\big( \binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}} \big) \right)= n - sk +s$ for all $n\ge sk$. This conjecture was previously proven for all even $s$, for $s \ge 4$ and large enough $n$, and for $k=2$. We prove the conjecture in the cases $s=3$ and $n$ large enough, or $k=s=3$. To this end, we prove versions of the Hilton-Milner theorem for $s$-stable sets. We also present a topological approach towards Meunier's conjecture.

inductive Formula (m : ℕ) where

/-!
# Non-well-founded proof graphs: a guarded negative result

This file separates three notions often conflated in discussions of circular proofs:
finite observations of a possibly infinite tree, cyclic proof graphs, and ordinary
hypothetical derivations.  Finite observations form a dcpo under inclusion.  In
contrast, requiring every dependency to have strictly smaller ordinal rank excludes
all cycles, so it cannot validate a genuinely self-referential proof.  Finally,
`P → P` has the usual finite assumption proof; circularity is unnecessary.
-/

namespace NonWellFoundedProofs

/-- A tiny implicational language. -/
inductive Formula (Atom : Type) where
  | atom : Atom → Formula Atom
  | imp : Formula Atom → Formula Atom → Formula Atom
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

infixr:55 " ⟹ " => Formula.imp

/-- Sequents carry a finite list of open assumptions. -/
structure Sequent (Atom : Type) where
  context : List (Formula Atom)
  conclusion : Formula Atom
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Ordinary finite natural-deduction proofs for implication. -/
inductive Derivation {Atom : Type} : Sequent Atom → Type
  | hyp {Γ A} (h : A ∈ Γ) : Derivation ⟨Γ, A⟩
  | impIntro {Γ A B} (d : Derivation ⟨A :: Γ, B⟩) :
      Derivation ⟨Γ, A ⟹ B⟩

/-- The canonical proof of `P → P`: introduce `P`, then use that assumption. -/
def identityDerivation {Atom : Type} (P : Formula Atom) :
    Derivation ⟨[], P ⟹ P⟩ :=
  .impIntro (.hyp (by simp))

/-- Height counts inference edges; an assumption leaf has height zero. -/
def Derivation.height {Atom : Type} {s : Sequent Atom} : Derivation s → ℕ
  | .hyp _ => 0
  | .impIntro d => d.height + 1

/-- The assumption proof of `P → P` has exactly height one. -/
theorem identityDerivation_height {Atom : Type} (P : Formula Atom) :
    (identityDerivation P).height = 1 := by
  simp [identityDerivation, Derivation.height]

/-- A potentially non-well-founded tree, represented extensionally by its finite
observations at addresses.  This is a final-coalgebra style encoding: no recursive
Lean value needs to contain itself, but labels may occur at every finite depth. -/
abbrev ProofTree (Label : Type) := List ℕ → Option Label

/-- A finite-depth approximation reveals nodes only through depth `n`. -/
def truncate {Label : Type} (n : ℕ) (t : ProofTree Label) : ProofTree Label :=
  fun p => if p.length ≤ n then t p else none

/-
Truncations agree with the original tree at every address eventually.
-/
theorem truncate_eventually {Label : Type} (t : ProofTree Label) (p : List ℕ) :
    truncate p.length t p = t p := by
  exact if_pos le_rfl

/-- The one-node cyclic graph unravels to a genuine infinite unary tree. -/
def selfUnravelling (Label : Type) (label : Label) : ProofTree Label :=
  fun p => if ∀ i ∈ p, i = 0 then some label else none

/-
Every address on the unary spine occurs in the cyclic graph's unravelling.
-/
theorem selfUnravelling_spine (Label : Type) (label : Label) (n : ℕ) :
    selfUnravelling Label label (List.replicate n 0) = some label := by
  unfold selfUnravelling; aesop;

/-
Therefore the unravelling has nodes at arbitrarily large finite depths.
-/
theorem selfUnravelling_unbounded (Label : Type) (label : Label) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : List ℕ, p.length = n ∧ selfUnravelling Label label p = some label := by
  exact ⟨List.replicate n 0, by simp, selfUnravelling_spine _ _ _⟩

/-- A finite observation is a set of labelled addresses in a proof tree.  Taking all
such sets also includes partial and inconsistent observations; consistency can be
imposed as a Scott-closed predicate separately. -/
abbrev Observation (Label : Type) := Set (List ℕ × Label)

/-- The limit of an increasing sequence of finite observations is their union. -/
def chainLimit {Label : Type} (c : ℕ → Observation Label) : Observation Label :=
  ⋃ n, c n

/-- Union is an upper bound of every stage. -/
theorem chain_le_limit {Label : Type} (c : ℕ → Observation Label) (n : ℕ) :
    c n ⊆ chainLimit c := by
  intro x hx
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, hx⟩

/-- Union is the least upper bound.  Thus observations, ordered by information
inclusion, are an ω-complete partial order (indeed a complete lattice). -/
theorem chainLimit_least {Label : Type} (c : ℕ → Observation Label)
    (u : Observation Label) (hu : ∀ n, c n ⊆ u) : chainLimit c ⊆ u := by
  intro x hx
  rcases Set.mem_iUnion.1 hx with ⟨n, hn⟩
  exact hu n hn

/-- A monotone sequence of observations. -/
def Increasing {Label : Type} (c : ℕ → Observation Label) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, c n ⊆ c (n + 1)

/-
Every finite stage of an increasing chain embeds into every later stage.
-/
theorem increasing_mono {Label : Type} {c : ℕ → Observation Label}
    (hc : Increasing c) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) : c m ⊆ c n := by
  exact monotone_nat_of_le_succ hc hmn

/-- A finite proof graph: `depends i j` says node `i` uses node `j` as a premise
or back-reference. -/
structure RankedGraph (Node : Type) where
  depends : Node → Node → Prop
  rank : Node → Ordinal
  decreases : ∀ {i j}, depends i j → rank j < rank i

/-
Strictly rank-decreasing dependencies cannot contain a self-reference.
-/
theorem no_self_reference {Node : Type} (G : RankedGraph Node) (i : Node) :
    ¬ G.depends i i := by
  exact fun h => G.decreases h |> lt_irrefl _

/-
Nor can a strictly decreasing dependency graph contain a finite directed cycle.
This directly disproves the proposed criterion "self-reference converges when it
occurs at a strictly smaller ordinal": returning to the same proof node forces its
ordinal to be strictly below itself.
-/
theorem no_ranked_cycle {Node : Type} (G : RankedGraph Node) (n : ℕ)
    (v : Fin (n + 1) → Node)
    (hedge : ∀ k : Fin n, G.depends (v k.castSucc) (v k.succ)) :
    ¬ G.depends (v (Fin.last n)) (v 0) := by
  have h_ind : ∀ k : Fin n, G.rank (v (Fin.succ k)) < G.rank (v (Fin.castSucc k)) := by
    exact fun k => G.decreases ( hedge k );
  have h_induction : ∀ k : Fin (n + 1), G.rank (v k) ≤ G.rank (v 0) := by
    intro k; induction' k using Fin.inductionOn with i IH; aesop; exact le_trans ( le_of_lt ( h_ind _ ) ) IH;
  exact fun h => not_lt_of_ge ( h_induction _ ) ( G.decreases h )

/-
A direct self-loop, the simplest purported circular proof, admits no decreasing
ordinal ranking.
-/
theorem self_loop_has_no_ranking (Node : Type) (i : Node)
    (depends : Node → Node → Prop) (hloop : depends i i) :
    ¬ ∃ rank : Node → Ordinal, ∀ {x y}, depends x y → rank y < rank x := by
  exact fun ⟨ rank, hr ⟩ => lt_irrefl _ ( hr hloop )

is extensionally equivalent to truth for `L`.  These two demanded fixed-point laws
are inconsistent.  This is the precise obstruction; it is not an "undefined
ordinal height" computation.
-/
theorem liar_fixed_point_impossible (Prov L : Prop)
    (reflection : Prov ↔ L) (liar : L ↔ ¬ Prov) : False := by
  grind

/-
Consequently no propositions can realize both liar self-reference and exact
reflection.
-/
theorem no_liar_model :
    ¬ ∃ Prov L : Prop, (Prov ↔ L) ∧ (L ↔ ¬ Prov) := by
  grind

# Future Directions

## Results established

The formalization distinguishes circular *syntax* from valid derivability.

1. **Finite observations do have limits.** Proof-tree observations are sets of labelled addresses. Their information order is inclusion, and `chainLimit` is union. The theorems `chain_le_limit` and `chainLimit_least` prove the expected least-upper-bound laws. This verifies the order-theoretic core of the proposed Scott-domain picture (the ambient observation space is actually a complete lattice).

2. **A cyclic graph can denote an infinite object.** `selfUnravelling` gives an extensional, non-well-founded unary tree. `selfUnravelling_spine` and `selfUnravelling_unbounded` prove that it has a node at every finite depth. This is a valid mathematical object, but that alone does not make it a sound proof.

3. **`P → P` has height one without circularity.** `identityDerivation` introduces `P` and closes the goal with the open assumption. `identityDerivation_height` proves its height is one. Calling this self-reference conflates a hypothesis occurrence with a back-edge to the theorem being proved.

4. **The strictly-smaller-ordinal convergence conjecture is disproved for cycles.** `no_self_reference`, `no_ranked_cycle`, and `self_loop_has_no_ranking` prove that a dependency cycle cannot admit an ordinal rank strictly decreasing along every edge. A return to the same node would force its rank to be strictly less than itself. Thus ordinal descent is a soundness condition precisely because it excludes genuine circularity; it does not resolve it.

5. **The liar cannot satisfy both exact reflection and its negating fixed-point equation.** `liar_fixed_point_impossible` and `no_liar_model` prove inconsistency of `Prov ↔ L` together with `L ↔ ¬Prov`. This is sharper than saying the liar has an “undefined height”: no propositions realize both equations in ordinary logic.

## Conjectures worth pursuing

### Guarded circularity via a later modality

Replace impossible strict rank decrease around a cycle by a guarded rule in which every back-reference lies beneath a “later” modality. The intended semantics should be step-indexed: validity at index `n + 1` may use the circular hypothesis only at index `n`. A useful target is a soundness theorem into streams of finite approximations.

### Scott-closed local correctness

The ambient observation lattice includes inconsistent partial trees. Define a local rule-correctness predicate and characterize conditions under which it is closed under directed unions. If all inference rules have finite arity and correctness is witnessed locally, directed-union preservation should follow; infinitary rules may provide counterexamples.

### Cyclic proof systems with a global trace condition

Ordinal descent on every edge is too strong. Established cyclic-proof methodology instead asks for progress infinitely often along each infinite branch. Formalize traces over graph unravellings and compare:

- local strict descent (which forbids every cycle),
- guarded step-index descent,
- Büchi-style infinite progress.

Prove soundness for a concrete inductive predicate before attempting general fixed-point logic.

### Separate syntax, semantics, and metatheory

A self-referential graph is finite syntax; its unravelling is a possibly infinite tree; validity is a semantic predicate. Future work should keep these three layers separate. The current results show that existence of a limit object does not imply proof-theoretic soundness.

### Incompleteness and arithmetization

The present liar theorem is propositional and does not formalize Gödel coding or a derivability predicate. A faithful incompleteness development would need syntax, substitution/diagonalization, a recursively axiomatized theory, and derivability conditions. Such infrastructure is necessary before making claims about Gödel incompleteness itself.

/-!
# Divisibility staircases

The proposed “Escher staircase” reverses inclusion: requiring values to be divisible
by larger powers produces a strictly *descending* chain.  This file proves that fact,
computes its intersection, and proves that an ascending chain automatically has its
first term as its intersection. It also records the Noetherian obstruction.
-/

namespace EscherStaircases

/-- The principal ideal of integers generated by `2^n`. -/
def dyadicIdeal (n : ℕ) : Ideal ℤ := Ideal.span {(2 : ℤ) ^ n}

/-- Successive dyadic ideals are strictly descending, not ascending. -/
theorem dyadicIdeal_strictAnti (n : ℕ) : dyadicIdeal (n + 1) < dyadicIdeal n := by
  refine' lt_of_le_of_ne _ _;
  · exact Ideal.span_singleton_le_span_singleton.mpr ( pow_dvd_pow _ n.le_succ );
  · have h_not_in : (2 : ℤ)^n ∉ dyadicIdeal (n + 1) := by
      rw [ dyadicIdeal, Ideal.mem_span_singleton ];
      exact_mod_cast Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt ( pow_pos ( by decide ) _ ) ( pow_lt_pow_right₀ ( by decide ) ( Nat.lt_succ_self _ ) );
    exact fun h => h_not_in <| h.symm ▸ Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self _

/-- Hence the dyadic ideals form an infinite strict descending chain. -/
theorem dyadicIdeal_strictAnti_of_lt {m n : ℕ} (h : m < n) :
    dyadicIdeal n < dyadicIdeal m := by
  induction h <;> simp_all +decide [dyadicIdeal];
  · convert dyadicIdeal_strictAnti m using 1;
  · exact lt_of_le_of_lt ( dyadicIdeal_strictAnti _ |> le_of_lt ) ‹_›

/-- No nonzero integer is divisible by every power of two. -/
theorem divisible_by_all_powers_two_eq_zero {z : ℤ}
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ, (2 : ℤ) ^ n ∣ z) : z = 0 := by
  by_contra h_nonzero
  have h_abs : ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ^ n > Int.natAbs z := by
    exact pow_unbounded_of_one_lt _ one_lt_two
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := h_abs
  have h_div : 2 ^ n ∣ z := by
    exact h n
  have h_abs_le : 2 ^ n ≤ Int.natAbs z := by
    exact Nat.le_of_dvd ( Int.natAbs_pos.mpr h_nonzero ) ( by simpa [ ← Int.natCast_dvd_natCast ] using h_div )
  linarith [hn]

/-- The intersection of all dyadic principal ideals is the zero ideal. -/
theorem iInf_dyadicIdeal : (⨅ n : ℕ, dyadicIdeal n) = ⊥ := by
  ext x;
  simp +decide [ dyadicIdeal, Ideal.mem_span_singleton ];
  exact ⟨ fun hx => divisible_by_all_powers_two_eq_zero hx, fun hx => by simp +decide [ hx ] ⟩

/-- The intersection of any ascending chain indexed from zero is its first ideal.
Thus equality with the first term is automatic, not an additional “looping” effect. -/
theorem monotone_iInf_eq_first
    {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (I : ℕ → Ideal R) (hmono : Monotone I) :
    (⨅ n, I n) = I 0 := by
  exact le_antisymm ( iInf_le _ _ ) ( le_iInf fun n => hmono ( Nat.zero_le n ) )

/-- In particular, every strictly ascending chain has intersection equal to its first
ideal; this condition cannot define a new height invariant. -/
theorem strictAscending_iInf_eq_first
    {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (I : ℕ → Ideal R)
    (hstrict : ∀ n, I n < I (n + 1)) : (⨅ n, I n) = I 0 := by
  apply monotone_iInf_eq_first;
  exact monotone_nat_of_le_succ fun n => le_of_lt ( hstrict n )

/-- A Noetherian ring admits no infinite strictly ascending sequence of ideals. -/
theorem noetherian_no_infinite_strictAscending
    {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : ℕ → Ideal R) :
    ¬ (∀ n, I n < I (n + 1)) := by
  by_contra! h;
  have h_strict_mono : StrictMono I := by
    exact strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ h;
  contrapose! h_strict_mono;
  exact not_strictMono_of_wellFoundedGT I

/-- Polynomial rings in finitely many variables are Noetherian and therefore have
no infinite strictly ascending chain of ideals. -/
theorem finite_mvPolynomial_no_infinite_strictAscending
    {k σ : Type*} [CommRing k] [IsNoetherianRing k] [Finite σ]
    (I : ℕ → Ideal (MvPolynomial σ k)) : ¬ (∀ n, I n < I (n + 1)) := by
  apply noetherian_no_infinite_strictAscending

/-- Integer-valued polynomial functions, represented extensionally as functions
`ℤ → ℤ` that agree with a rational polynomial on every integer. -/
def intPolynomialFunctions : Subring (ℤ → ℤ) where
  carrier := {f | ∃ p : Polynomial ℚ, ∀ z : ℤ, p.eval (z : ℚ) = (f z : ℚ)}
  zero_mem' := ⟨0, by simp⟩
  one_mem' := ⟨1, by simp⟩
  add_mem' := by
    rintro f g ⟨p, hp⟩ ⟨q, hq⟩
    exact ⟨p + q, by simp [hp, hq]⟩
  mul_mem' := by
    rintro f g ⟨p, hp⟩ ⟨q, hq⟩
    exact ⟨p * q, by simp [hp, hq]⟩
  neg_mem' := by
    rintro f ⟨p, hp⟩
    exact ⟨-p, by simp [hp]⟩

/-- Integer-valued polynomial functions whose values are all divisible by `2^n`. -/
def intValuedDyadicIdeal (n : ℕ) : Ideal intPolynomialFunctions where
  carrier := {f | ∀ z : ℤ, (2 : ℤ) ^ n ∣ f.1 z}
  zero_mem' := by simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg z
    exact dvd_add (hf z) (hg z)
  smul_mem' := by
    intro f g hg z
    exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hg z) (f.1 z)

/-- The proposed ideals in the ring of integer-valued polynomial functions are
strictly descending as the exponent grows. -/
theorem intValuedDyadicIdeal_strictAnti (n : ℕ) :
    intValuedDyadicIdeal (n + 1) < intValuedDyadicIdeal n := by
  refine' ⟨ fun f hf z => dvd_trans _ ( hf z ), _ ⟩;
  · exact pow_dvd_pow _ n.le_succ;
  · refine' Set.not_subset.2 ⟨ _, _, _ ⟩;
    exact ⟨ fun _ => 2 ^ n, ⟨ Polynomial.C ( 2 ^ n : ℚ ), by simp +decide ⟩ ⟩;
    · exact fun _ => dvd_rfl;
    · intro h; have := h 0; norm_num at this;
      exact absurd this ( mod_cast Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt ( pow_pos ( by decide ) _ ) ( pow_lt_pow_right₀ ( by decide ) ( Nat.lt_succ_self _ ) ) )

/-- Their infinite intersection consists only of the zero polynomial function. -/
theorem iInf_intValuedDyadicIdeal :
    (⨅ n : ℕ, intValuedDyadicIdeal n) = ⊥ := by
  ext; simp [Submodule.mem_iInf];
  constructor <;> intro h <;> simp_all +decide [ intValuedDyadicIdeal ];
  rename_i f; exact Subtype.ext <| funext fun z => divisible_by_all_powers_two_eq_zero fun n => h n z;
